prompt:
You are a sceptical financial analyst reviewing a forecast prepared by a colleague.

Given the following forecast for PFC (base year 2021):
{
  "strategy": "alt_strategy",
  "base_year": 2021,
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "forecast": [
    {
      "year": 2022,
      "revenue_cr": 78500,
      "net_income_cr": 13800,
      "eps": 52.27
    },
    {
      "year": 2023,
      "revenue_cr": 86500,
      "net_income_cr": 15200,
      "eps": 57.57
    },
    {
      "year": 2024,
      "revenue_cr": 95200,
      "net_income_cr": 16800,
      "eps": 63.63
    }
  ],
  "top_assumptions": [
    "Loan book growth of approximately 10-12% per annum drives interest income (the dominant revenue component at ~99% of total), supported by PFC's continued lending to the power sector with gross loans growing from ~7.2 lakh crore in FY2021; NPA reduction (Gross NPA fell from 8.08% to 5.70% in FY2021) supports lower credit costs and better PAT quality going forward.",
    "Net profit normalization assumed: FY2021 PAT of Rs 15,716 crore was exceptionally high (65.8% YoY jump from Rs 9,477 crore in FY2020) partly due to significantly lower deferred tax expense and large write-back of provisions on Stage III loans (reduction of Rs 5,521 crore in Stage III loans); FY2022 PAT is projected lower at Rs 13,800 crore as one-off benefits normalize, with gradual recovery thereafter driven by loan book expansion and improving asset quality."
  ],
  "reasoning": "PFC is an NBFC, so Total Revenue from Operations (Interest Income + Dividend + Fees + Other Operating Income) is used as the top-line: FY2021 = Rs 71,656 crore vs FY2020 = Rs 62,189 crore, a 15.2% YoY growth. However, FY2021 PAT of Rs 15,716 crore was anomalously high (up 65.8% YoY) due to a very large deferred tax credit of Rs 1,549 crore (vs a deferred tax charge of Rs 1,527 crore in FY2020), significant Stage III loan write-backs reducing provisioning benefits, and favorable exchange movements (translation loss dropped from Rs 4,991 crore to Rs 166 crore); these are non-recurring tailwinds. Revenue growth of ~15% is above the estimated 3-5 year CAGR of ~11-12% for an infrastructure-focused NBFC of this scale, so a blended ~10% revenue CAGR is used for projections with mean-reversion in PAT margins. The loan book grew ~11.7% YoY (from Rs 6.46 lakh crore to Rs 7.22 lakh crore), and management's focus on the power sector with ongoing capex-linked disbursements supports steady mid-double-digit revenue growth, while high leverage (debt-to-equity ~8.5x) constrains aggressive expansion but is normal for an NBFC of this type."
}

Step 1: Identify the 3 most critical assumptions embedded in this forecast.
Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).

RESPONSE FORMAT: Begin your response DIRECTLY with the opening brace { — no reasoning or text before the JSON.

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "company": "<COMPANY>",
  "base_year": <YYYY>,
  "strategy": "<baseline|alt_strategy>",
  "assumptions": [
    {"assumption": "<text>", "failure_scenario": "<text>", "risk": "<Low|Medium|High>"}
  ],
  "confidence_score": <0-100>,
  "overall_critique": "<2 sentences>"
}
